title: Crossed-product data for a cocycle
statement: For any field K and any homogeneous continuous degree-two cocycle z of its absolute Galois group with coefficients in the discrete units of its separable closure (def-sc-galois-units-cohomology), there exist a central simple K-algebra A, a nonzero matrix size n, a separable-closure matrix splitting e, and locally constant invertible matrix lifts b satisfying the descent equation and with scalar defect exactly galoisUnitsCocycleValue K z (def-sc-brauer-scalar-defect).

source.place: The crossed-product construction following Lemma 03R6 and Theorem 03R7

proof.text: Use [lem-sc-cocycle-monomial-coefficients] to obtain n nonzero, a permutation homomorphism p, and unit weights w with a locally constant paired map and the prescribed twisted coefficient identity. Its proof constructs the regular representation from finite quotient data.

Construct b(g) as the monomial matrix with (i,j) entry w(g,j) when i=p(g)j and zero otherwise. Its inverse has (i,j) entry w(g,i) inverse when p(g)i=j and zero otherwise. In each inverse product, the finite sum has a single possible nonzero summand, which is a unit times its inverse. Local constancy follows by postcomposing the paired map. Compute b(g) g(b(h)) columnwise: the only nonzero summand is at p(h)j and its coefficient is w(g,p(h)j)g(w(h,j)). The coefficient identity and p(gh)=p(g)p(h) give the scalar-defect equation.

At g=h=1, the defect equation gives b(1)b(1)=scalar(c(1,1))b(1); cancel b(1) to obtain a scalar identity matrix. Thus conjugation is the identity at 1. Entrywise mapping preserves matrix products. For general g,h, compose conjugations, combine b(g)g(b(h)) and its inverse, substitute the scalar defect, and commute and cancel the scalar. This proves T_g T_h=T_(gh) by a real matrix calculation, without normalization.

Apply [lem-sc-projective-matrix-descent] to the explicitly constructed b and the proved local constancy and action laws. It supplies A and the splitting e with the required descent equation for this same b. Combine that equation with the already proved scalar defect and nonzero n to give the original witnesses.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 03R7 and Section 0DVG; regular monomial matrices, invertibility, prescribed scalar defect, and cancellation to a genuine action proved in Lean by V1; finite quotient and invariant-algebra descent separated
